throughput_requirements: Min guaranteed sustained throughput: 60,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across cluster) during market hours (08:30-16:00 ET)
Concurrency cap target: 64 active request streams with average sequence length 350 tokens
Burst policy requested: allow spikes up to 150,000 tokens/sec for 10 minutes with graceful shedding after 12 minutes
Desired latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for requests up to 512 tokens; p99 <= 900ms
KV cache expectations: prefix caching for market-context windows, reduce upstream tokens by ~30% for repeated queries
reserved_gpu_planning: Target GPU fleet: mix of 8 x H100 (primary low-latency lanes) + 12 x A10G (cost-effective batching)
Autoscale rules: reserve baseline for 60k tps; burst pool spun from committed capacity + short-term borrowable nodes
Quantization plan: use 4-bit quantized model variants for non-critical rerank paths to increase throughput
Throughput modelling: Redwood provided token/sec projections per GPU (H100 ~7.5k tps steady for 512 tokens with batching)
sla_negotiation_points: Define measurement windows and how tokens/sec is measured (ingress vs generated) — PLR insists on server-side generated token accounting
Credit formula request: sliding-window percent shortfall (30-day lookback) with credit bands (5%,10%,25%)
Maintenance windows: max 4 hours/mo with advance notice; PLR wants blackout exceptions for earnings days
Failover guarantees: automated fallback to compatible model variants w/ documented quality delta and no-penalty invocation
Penalty cap: PLR requests monthly credit up to 20% of committed spend for repeated SLA misses — Redwood requested negotiation to 10% cap
